first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ and activation is down 6% QoQ, both of which align directly with prior positive results from onboarding simplification (memory_86, memory_31) that improved completion, time-to-value, and first-week activation without noted downstream harm. Given only one experiment slot, this action addresses two current metric declines simultaneously and has a track record of durable, non-retention-damaging lift. Promotional pricing is tempting given competitor pressure on price-sensitive SMBs, but memory_73 explicitly warns it boosts acquisition/revenue while materially harming 30-day retention and should not be generalized as a growth response—pursuing it now would trade long-term qualified revenue for short-term defensive gains, conflicting with the stated objective. I verified memory_86 and memory_31 since they are the load-bearing evidence for the chosen action; verifying memory_73 was unnecessary since its cautionary framing is already explicit and sufficient to deprioritize promotional pricing this cycle. Scaling as a standard experiment (not broad rollout) preserves ability to observe onboarding-specific effects before wider deployment, and keeps optionality open for next cycle to reassess competitive pricing response or activation messaging.
